prompt:
Reddit post, r/houseplants.
Title: Heeeey reddit wtf is that and why isn't alcohol working?

This was my very first syngonium. I absolutely will. Not. Lose. It. It started my love for syngoniums and i just cannot lose it. I have sprayed this thing down so many times in the last few weeks. I've used peroxide, alcohol, insecticide, neem, I tried fungicide as a last ditch! What is is and how to I make them disappear!?

I've had a nasty mealy problem for the last year ish but haven't lost a plant yet. These didn't look like mealies to I wasn't too sure what to do and everything either reeks and isn't working or smells slightly better and still isn't working.

What is wrong with my plant?
answer:
**Most likely: young mealybugs.** Those tiny fuzzy white specks are juveniles that haven't grown the adults' cottony coat yet. That's no surprise after a year of mealies.

**Why spraying isn't working:** their wax repels water-based sprays, and alcohol evaporates in seconds. No spray reaches the eggs and adults hiding in the papery sheaths at the base, the pot rim, the soil, or your other plants, so new ones keep hatching. Dead ones also stay stuck on, so specks that are still there don't mean the spray failed. Only new specks after wiping mean they're still active.

**Could also be:**
- **Armored scale:** tiny white dashes that alcohol can't get through. Poke one with a toothpick. A mealybug squishes into a wet smear, while scale pops off as a hard little shell.
- **Thrips larvae:** pale yellowish slivers that scurry when touched, plus silvery patches with black dots on the leaves.

**Fix:**
1. **Wipe, don't spray.** Rinse off the old residue in the shower. Then wipe every leaf (both sides) and stem with cotton pads dipped in 1:1 rubbing alcohol and water plus a drop of dish soap. Use a cotton swab with undiluted alcohol in the base sheaths, and cut off the worst leaves. Check the roots too: white fluff there means wash them and repot in fresh soil.
2. **Add a systemic.** Imidacloprid or acetamiprid granules or sticks (where legal) kick in within 1–2 weeks, reach bugs you can't, and last 6–8 weeks. Without one, use insecticidal soap every 5–7 days for 6 weeks to catch each hatch. If it turns out to be scale, use horticultural oil instead.
3. **Stop the cocktail.** Peroxide and fungicide don't kill insects. Layering alcohol, neem and everything else is likely behind some of the dead leaves.
4. **Isolate it and treat your whole collection** on the same schedule, or they'll keep coming back.

The stems are firm and it's pushing new shoots, so it's very saveable.
